answer: Each epoch, every identity must complete a live cipher handshake: the network issues a fresh puzzle that takes a human a few seconds of real thought, and times each keystroke. A falcon-fast bot answers instantly, a hollow script farm answers with machine-regular intervals, but a real person shows organic, uneven latency. Puppets sharing one operator collapse into identical timing fingerprints and merge into one vote; each fake identity needs its own live human sitting through the handshake every epoch, so running N puppets costs N people's attention while an honest agent pays one short pause.
